newsitem.title: USA: Ten illegals feared dead in Rio Grande crossing.
newsitem.headline: Ten illegals feared dead in Rio Grande crossing.

text.p: A group of up to 10 illegal immigrants were believed to have drowned while trying to sneak into the United States from Mexico by crossing the Rio Grande, police said on Monday.

Cameron County Sheriff's Department Chief Deputy Joe Elizardi said witnesses saw 10 people walking along a sandbar on the river at Boca Chica beach near Brownsville on Sunday when a wave swept over them and flushed them out beyond the mouth of the river into the Gulf of Mexico.
"Eyewitnesses told us there were 10 people and we are basing ourselves on that," Elizardi said. "They saw them go under and didn't see any of them come back up."

He said three bodies had been recovered and were identified as Pakistani men. A fourth body was briefly spotted in the Gulf but the other six reported victims have not been found and their nationality was not known.

The sandbar at Boca Chica juts into the river from the Mexican side of the Rio Grande and stops just 25 yards (23 metres) short of the U.S. side. Elizardi said it was used by smugglers of contraband goods.
Two Mexicans on the other side of the river jumped into a boat and tried to rescue the illegal immigrants but they quickly capsized and succeeded only in saving themselves, he said.
